races.name: L & R Pest Control Services Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Races prominently and has every chance to control this from the front; two recent seconds on Good ground show consistency, and Iain Jardine's yard is 2/35 in the last 14 days — respectable strike rate but not firing at top clip; eight days since last run is fine for a horse in form.|

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the same Jardine yard as Newport, returning after exactly 14 days including two flat runs; four placings from 15 Good-ground starts signals competence rather than authority in these conditions, and racing at the back of this field could make it difficult to find a clear run.|

runners_data.name: Betteryouthanme
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with an excellent Good-ground profile — one win and one place from five attempts — and a recent third at 20f suggests the 2m trip is within range; William Maggs takes the ride for R Mike Smith's yard, which has had just one winner from nine runners in 14 days, so yard form is a mild watch.|

runners_data.name: Theirshegoes
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine campaigns, fitted with a p-hood, but a run of 28 days off and a form string showing a fall and three finishes outside the top five is hard to work with; hold-up style in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to set it up for closers is a tactical concern.|

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Drawn into prominent position on historical form, but all five recent runs came on Soft and all were at 20f — both the Going and the distance drop to 2m on Good represent genuine queries; Mark Walford's yard has been active (3/11 in 14 days) and the p-hood suggests keenness management.|

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: A prominent type returning from 44 days off, having pulled up last time on a Flat run 19 days into that break; one win and four places in similar-going code runs hints at a horse who is consistent when fit, but fitness on return after a hurdles absence is the key unknown here.|

runners_data.name: Snapaudaciaheros
runners_data.note: Two wins over this exact 16f/Good combination make the form credentials stand out, but this horse is a genuine front-runner whose natural position is up with Newport — pushed back to midfield by the field's pace surplus, racing out of role will blunt the effectiveness of those sharp course-and-distance wins; p-hood and tp-hood noted.|

runners_data.name: Curious Mrs Fox
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has not finished better than sixth in her last four runs, including twice on Good ground at 16f; David Thompson's yard is 0/5 in 14 days and Joshua Thompson's claim may not be enough to compensate for a lack of recent form or tactical position.|

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old who has placed second or third in four of his last five starts, mostly on Good and Soft — consistent without winning; this horse is a natural prominent racer displaced to midfield by the crowded pace positions, and at his age racing further back than usual may cost him the decisive moment in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Knockeranna Rose
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up tactics are this mare's trademark — a second and two thirds in her recent profile on Good-and-Soft ground show she stays well; 39 days since last run is the notable flag, and she needs the pace to be truly honest to generate enough momentum from off the bridle to threaten.|

runners_data.name: Bouboule
runners_data.note: The youngest runner in the field at four, fitted with tp-hood, returning from 14 days including a Flat run; a form string of 355P-7 on Good ground with zero wins and two places out of 15 Good outings makes this a difficult confidence bet — a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield for space reasons, and Leah Noreci's 7lb claim does not obviously compensate.|

races.paceDynamic: Newport is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger looking to push for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m trip on Good ground at Hexham. Betteryouthanme and Huit Reflets are the natural prominent types most likely to sit directly behind Newport and fill the early positions two and three, while Top Flight Century will also be keen to race close to the pace. The field contains a surplus of horses who prefer to race prominently — Snapaudaciaheros and Malangen are genuine front-running/prominent types who are mapped to midfield precisely because Newport and Betteryouthanme are likely to take those berths first, meaning those two will race further back than ideal and their chances are compromised accordingly. With one controlled pace-setter setting an honest but unforced tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the leader who can travel within themselves and pounce before the hold-up horses can generate a meaningful late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Newport Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Newport bowls along at a fair but unforced pace with Betteryouthanme and Huit Reflets tracking close.
scenarios.body: If Newport bowls along at a fair but unforced pace with Betteryouthanme and Huit Reflets tracking close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Rally On Easy Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely pedestrian early, allowing hold-up horses to close the gap turning for home.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is genuinely pedestrian early, allowing hold-up horses to close the gap turning for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surplus Pace Causes Friction
scenarios.trigger: If Snapaudaciaheros or Malangen push forward aggressively from their mapped midfield positions and inject unexpected pace.
scenarios.body: If Snapaudaciaheros or Malangen push forward aggressively from their mapped midfield positions and inject unexpected pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Newport is completely unchallenged, sets his own fractions, and the field simply cannot run him down from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Newport is completely unchallenged, sets his own fractions, and the field simply cannot run him down from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Newport's early tempo is the race-shaper — if Tom Midgley settles him into a genuinely comfortable rhythm unchallenged, the race belongs to those tracking closest, so watch Betteryouthanme and Huit Reflets for early position.

Snapaudaciaheros and Malangen are natural front-runners displaced into midfield — if either pushes forward at the start to reclaim their preferred ground, the pace dynamic changes abruptly and a stronger-run race develops.

Huit Reflets has run exclusively on Soft in recent outings at 20f — the switch to Good ground and a shorter 2m trip is an unproven combination for this horse and connections, and a below-par run would not be a surprise.

Top Flight Century is returning from 44 days off with a mid-break Flat run included — watch how sharply it moves in the first few hurdles to gauge whether it is truly fit enough to sustain its prominent style to the line.

Mr Lincoln and Knockeranna Rose are both dependent on a slow early pace to bring their hold-up styles into play — if Newport sets even a moderate tempo, both are effectively racing for minor honours at best.

races.name: Chris Lowther & Brian Ellison 28 Years Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Beyond The Verge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Susan Corbett returning after 435 days off; won over Good in similar company and showed placing form, but the long absence is the key risk here and he needs to strip fit first time out.

runners_data.name: Getaway Vic
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse with strong form on Good ground including two second-place finishes in longer-trip handicaps; Shane Fenelon claims 5lb and ran just two days ago which is an unusual pattern worth monitoring, but the form profile suits this trip well.

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rocco
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a question mark as a style unknown; 353 days off the track and only one run on similar going, making him an enigma for pace-mapping purposes — Patrick Neville's small yard rarely sends them long distances without a fair chance.

runners_data.name: Teofimo
runners_data.note: J S Bolger-trained three-year-old whose form shows finishes in the 6-8 range and a fall; his true style is hold-up but the crowded rear means he will likely race closer to midfield than ideal, and at STYLE_FIT 0.90 his chance is trimmed in shapes that depend on that rearward position.

runners_data.name: Run Happy
runners_data.note: Another style unknown, lightly raced and pulled up on last start; the Easterby yard is active (T14: 5/34) and he ran 12 days ago suggesting a quick return, but the P on his form string and limited data make him unreliable in pace terms.

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: Has only ever finished outside the top three on Good ground and Patrick Neville runs two in this race; her genuine style is hold-up but with the rear congested she will find herself racing in midfield against her natural instincts, which the 0.90 STYLE_FIT flag reflects.

runners_data.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners_data.note: William Young Jnr runner who comes in fresh enough (29 days) with one run on Good showing a seventh; genuine hold-up type, best served by an honest pace scenario, but the form to date offers nothing compelling to suggest she can improve sufficiently.

runners_data.name: Frisky Whiskey
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner (home trainer advantage at Hexham) has gone 6-6 in two starts on Good, both over shorter trips than today's 2m4f; the step up in distance is the key question, and the headgear flag alongside the consistent back-of-field style suggests she needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Loman Lady
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, trained by Dan Skelton (T14: 14/28, outstanding strike rate) and ridden by Harry Skelton; won last time over 2m on Good and is well placed to dictate from the front — the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is racing slightly out of her optimal role at the head of affairs in a maiden, but the stable form is compelling.

runners_data.name: Millena Agent
runners_data.note: Mark Walford runner who finished third over 3m on Good last time; wears headgear (p), style unknown but the longer trip last run suggests stamina is there — Jamie Hamilton is a good booking for Hexham and the place form is the best angle here.

runners_data.name: Rachel Lopez
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan rides for Stuart Coltherd; showed a second-place finish on soft and a third over 2m on Good, making her one of the more exposed hold-up types with a legitimate form line at this sort of trip and ground combination.

races.paceDynamic: Loman Lady is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Harry Skelton in the saddle for the in-form Dan Skelton yard, she is likely to stride on and set a measured, uncontested gallop over this 2m4f trip on Good ground at Hexham. Beyond The Verge and Getaway Vic are the nearest prominent challengers, but neither carries the same natural pace-setting profile, meaning the early fractions are unlikely to be pressured and the tempo will be controlled from the front. This race shape — a lone leader setting a sustainable pace — classically suits horses that can track close to the front and pick off the leader when the race begins to quicken in the final two hurdles, putting a premium on prominent-to-midfield stalkers over true closers. The field contains more hold-up types (Dolly Dior, Teofimo) than the map can accommodate at the rear; Loman Lady and Getaway Vic are best placed to secure their natural positions, while Dolly Dior and Teofimo are unlikely to be as far back as their redistribution implies, adding mild midfield congestion but not disrupting the front end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Loman Lady Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Loman Lady goes forward uncontested and controls the tempo from the front, setting a sustainable pace that keeps the field strung out.
scenarios.body: If Loman Lady goes forward uncontested and controls the tempo from the front, setting a sustainable pace that keeps the field strung out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Loman Lady's gallop is just honest enough that a prominent tracker can cruise into contention and overhaul her between the last two hurdles.
scenarios.body: If Loman Lady's gallop is just honest enough that a prominent tracker can cruise into contention and overhaul her between the last two hurdles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the front two exhaust each other and a fresh-legged midfield type gets a run through to score.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the front two exhaust each other and a fresh-legged midfield type gets a run through to score.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a true hold-up horse can produce a sustained late run from the back to catch a tiring field.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses late and a true hold-up horse can produce a sustained late run from the back to catch a tiring field.

watchPoints.text: Watch Loman Lady's jumping — if Harry Skelton gets into an uncontested rhythm she could dictate entirely, but any early blunder could unsettle the front-running plan and compress the field behind her.

Getaway Vic ran just two days ago, which is an unusually quick turnaround; monitor his market move and early behaviour in the paddock as fitness or freshness concerns could compromise a horse who otherwise profiles well for this race shape.

Dolly Dior and Teofimo are both natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map — if multiple horses attempt to fill the same ground between the 7th and 9th hurdles, interference or traffic problems become more likely than average.

Beyond The Verge returns after a 435-day absence; a prominent-running horse coming back fresh at Hexham can either strip ready or need the run, and his market move at the off will be informative about stable confidence.

Redbridge Rocco and Run Happy are both style unknowns in a race where the shape is otherwise fairly readable — if either jumps with early fluency they could slot in closer to the pace than expected and influence the race from the front more than the data suggests.

races.name: Matfen Hall Hotel Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Parisencore
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Nicky Richards — 37 days off, 10 years old but consistent on Good going (9/15 comparable runs); STYLE_FIT flag is mild here as leading is his role, though he races at OR 125 off a top weight of 168lbs which could blunt his resolve late.

runners_data.name: Cossack Chach
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a 211-day absence for James Moffatt (trainer 0/6 last 14 days) is the primary flag — tongue-tie/cheekpieces noted; has won over this trip on Good and showed smart form but the long layoff at a novice-ish age introduces real uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Kientzheim
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes a confident booking for Ben Haslam; placed in his last two on Good/Soft and won over 20f on Soft — the 17f trip is proven and recent form is solid, making him a natural second-string prominent type likely to secure his berth behind Parisencore.

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who landed a 16f Good-ground win 15 days ago for the in-form Sam England yard; tongue-bar fitted, travels smoothly off the pace, and the Hexham finish suits a horse who wants to be delivered late — well-weighted at OR 115.

runners_data.name: Cobbler's Boy
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton in excellent current form (T14: 12/24); tongue-tie fitted, six-year-old with consecutive placings and a recent win on Good at 17f — his hold-up profile maps perfectly to this moderate-pace scenario and his sim-going record (4/11) understates solid placed form.

runners_data.name: Herja
runners_data.note: Patrick Griffin's charge has placed five times in 13 Good-ground starts and is a natural prominent racer — but with the field stacked with front-minded types, he is most likely pushed back rather than racing where he wants; form shows consistency without a decisive win, and the OR 106 mark gives him something to work with if he does find cover.

runners_data.name: Conquer The Breeze
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins last time out (16f Good, 16f Soft) for Adam Nicol, and lightly weighted at OR 102 — but he wants to race prominently and the congested pace map means he is likely crowded out; his style-fit concern (0.90) is the most acute in the field and punters should factor that into any assessment of his chance replicating recent form.

races.paceDynamic: Parisencore is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press hard from the off, he should dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m7½f trip on Good ground at Hexham. Kientzheim, Cossack Chach, Herja, and Conquer The Breeze all carry prominent tendencies, but with more pace-inclined runners than the race shape can accommodate, Herja and Conquer The Breeze are the most likely to be squeezed back from their natural position — Kientzheim and Cossack Chach, with stronger claims to rank and experience, are better placed to actually secure prominent berths behind Parisencore. The result is a structured, relatively unhurried gallop that is unlikely to stretch the field early, meaning stamina reserves remain largely intact until the climb to the Hexham finish. This shape favours hold-up runners and those able to travel smoothly just off the pace, as the moderate tempo will not blunt closers — Glory And Honour and Cobbler's Boy are the profiles best positioned to exploit a well-controlled early fractions race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Parisencore Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore leads at a measured gallop and hold-up runners conserve enough to challenge off the final bend.
scenarios.body: If Parisencore leads at a measured gallop and hold-up runners conserve enough to challenge off the final bend.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Kientzheim or Cossack Chach travel prominently and prove strong enough to wear down a tired Parisencore in the final stages.
scenarios.body: If Kientzheim or Cossack Chach travel prominently and prove strong enough to wear down a tired Parisencore in the final stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore jumps boldly, steals a significant lead, and converts his controlled fractions into an outstaying performance.
scenarios.body: If Parisencore jumps boldly, steals a significant lead, and converts his controlled fractions into an outstaying performance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Herja or Conquer The Breeze force their way into prominent positions and create a faster-than-expected pace that scrambles the race.
scenarios.body: If Herja or Conquer The Breeze force their way into prominent positions and create a faster-than-expected pace that scrambles the race.

watchPoints.text: Cossack Chach returning after 211 days — watch his odds move in the market as a sharp move in would signal strong homework, while a drift would confirm the layoff concern is real.

Herja and Conquer The Breeze may attempt to push forward at the start despite the redistribution — if either forces their way into a prominent position and accelerates the pace, the hold-up horses' winning chance narrows sharply.

Parisencore carries 168lbs as a 10-year-old and if he begins to make jumping errors or weakens after the second-last, Danny McMenamin may be unable to hold off challengers on the final climb — watch his jumping in the back straight.

Glory And Honour ran just 15 days ago — watch early market moves for any trainer confidence signals, as the quick turnaround for a 10-year-old on Good ground is worth monitoring for any signs of freshness or fatigue.

Hexham's finish is a testing uphill straight that consistently stretches tired horses — any runner who has been asked for early effort to secure position (particularly Herja or Conquer The Breeze if pushed wide) may find the final two fences arriving at the worst moment.

races.name: Jethro's Cafe Of Haltwhistle Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Perseus Way
runners_data.note: Three wins from three on Good going, all in the last eight months, gives this seven-year-old a compelling profile for today's conditions; Harry Reed returns after an eight-day break, and the hold-up style is perfectly calibrated for a race where High Dancer will set the tempo.

runners_data.name: High Dancer
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards has had no runners in the last 14 days and Danny McMenamin partners a horse that has won twice from four runs on Good — front-running here is straightforward but the 0/6 T14 strike rate is worth noting; the confirmed pace angle gives it a structural advantage, though it operates out of its most natural comfort zone as a broader prominent type.

runners_data.name: Haarar
runners_data.note: Sam England's yard has two winners from 14 recent runners and Jonathan England takes the ride on a horse that hasn't run for 82 days (34 days filtered), with all five recent runs on Soft — the switch to Good is a genuine question mark, and all five historical entries show Soft or worse, so the going is an untested variable.

runners_data.name: Winds Of Winter
runners_data.note: George Bewley's eight-year-old is naturally a prominent racer but finds itself squeezed out of that position by High Dancer's prior claim in this small field; Conor Rabbitt claims 3lbs, which softens the weight, but the horse's best form comes when bowling along in front — racing in a more restrained role tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Well Educated
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with three consecutive runner-up finishes, all on Good or Good-equivalent ground and all over trips between 2m and 2m4f — the profile is consistent but the win has eluded it across 15 similar-going starts; Jonathon Bewley partners for a yard with 0 wins from 5 recent runners.

races.paceDynamic: High Dancer is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival looking to press from the outset, Danny McMenamin can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Hexham. Haarar and Winds Of Winter are both prominent types by inclination, but with High Dancer already occupying that position and the field small enough that crowding at the front becomes awkward, at least one of them will be racing somewhat out of their natural comfort zone. This field contains more pace than the race shape can accommodate — Winds Of Winter is the redistriubted prominent type most likely to find itself racing in a more restrained role than it would naturally choose, with Haarar the likelier of the two to at least track High Dancer closely. A controlled, honest gallop on Good ground over 2m at Hexham is a shape that classically suits hold-up horses with a clean turn of foot — Perseus Way and Well Educated, both genuine hold-up types with strong recent form on similar going, are the profiles that benefit most from High Dancer setting an honest but manageable tempo into which they can close.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: High Dancer Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If High Dancer leads unchallenged at a comfortable clip and the prominent types settle respectfully behind.
scenarios.body: If High Dancer leads unchallenged at a comfortable clip and the prominent types settle respectfully behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Haarar or Winds Of Winter pushes up to press High Dancer, injecting more pace than anticipated.
scenarios.body: If Haarar or Winds Of Winter pushes up to press High Dancer, injecting more pace than anticipated.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If High Dancer dawdles and the field concertinas entering the final circuit, producing a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If High Dancer dawdles and the field concertinas entering the final circuit, producing a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Good ground rides faster than expected and the hold-up horses cannot bridge the gap set by an assured front-runner.
scenarios.body: If Good ground rides faster than expected and the hold-up horses cannot bridge the gap set by an assured front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Haarar or Winds Of Winter attempts to press High Dancer in the early stages — if either does, the pace rises sharply and the race shape flips in favour of the closers more decisively.

Haarar's going record is entirely on Soft or worse; if Good rides firm enough to inconvenience it at any point in the race, its chance diminishes significantly and it may fade from a prominent position.

Well Educated has placed three times in a row without winning — watch whether it travels strongly enough to challenge from the last flight or simply delivers the same placed effort it has made a habit of.
High Dancer's trainer Nicky Richards has sent out zero winners from six runners in the last 14 days — monitor market moves to gauge stable confidence heading into this race.

Perseus Way arrives on an eight-day turnaround having won over course-relevant trips on Good — watch for early market support as a guide to whether connections are bullish after the quick reappearance.

races.name: Tynedale Function Suite Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ostend
runners_data.note: Controls from the front at Hexham with a decent record on Good going (2W4P from six similar-ground runs), though OR 112 and top weight of 170lbs is a stiff ask; Shane Fenelon (5lb claimer) helps offset that, but the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution if race dynamics push him out of his lead role.

runners_data.name: Buddah Castle
runners_data.note: Returned a winner last time on Good over 2m on similar ground, but 94 days off since and only three runs in similar conditions (no wins, no places) is a concern; Brian Hughes is an obvious positive and the 6yo may strip fitter, but the layoff is the key watch point.

runners_data.name: Moodofthemoment
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with headgear (p) and strong recent form at this trip, including a win on Good 20f and placed runs in similar conditions; David Thompson's yard is out of form in the last 14 days (0/3), which tempers optimism despite the horse's fitness (28 days since last run).

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride for in-form Dan Skelton (12/26 over 14 days) on a horse with a consistent placed record, all recent runs at 20-22f on Good or Soft; the step to 2m4f at Hexham is marginally unexplored territory but his record of placing in nearly every recent start makes him a live each-way factor.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Three-timer in progress with wins on Good over the same distance (24f, 20f, 20f) — form could hardly be more relevant; headgear (t) is retained and Jonathan England knows the horse well, making him the most obvious threat to Ostend if he can lead or sit prominently throughout.

runners_data.name: West Lawn
runners_data.note: OR 84 means he gets in light at 142lbs, and he owns solid course and distance form at Hexham over 24f including a recent win; by nature a prominent racer, but Ostend and Passengerontheship mean he is unlikely to secure that position here, which blunts his chance considerably.

races.paceDynamic: Ostend is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Passengerontheship as a second prominent type to challenge for early position, he should be able to control this race from the front without being seriously pressured. Passengerontheship has been in excellent recent form with three consecutive wins and will want to race handy, meaning Ostend cannot simply coast — but the pace should still be sustainable rather than frenetic over 2m4f on Good ground at Hexham. West Lawn is a natural prominent racer who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because Ostend and Passengerontheship occupy the front positions; this field holds more prominent-types than can all secure their favoured spot, and Ostend is most likely to lead with Passengerontheship immediately behind. This race shape — a controlled, single-led pace with one serious challenger close up — strongly favours prominent-to-handy types who can travel just off the leader and produce a clean round of jumping, rather than hold-up horses who will face a difficult task bridging the gap from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ostend Controls, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ostend leads at a fair clip and the pace proves honest enough to stretch the hold-up horses but not burn out the prominent types.
scenarios.body: If Ostend leads at a fair clip and the pace proves honest enough to stretch the hold-up horses but not burn out the prominent types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Ostend goes too steady and sets an insufficient gallop, allowing hold-up horses to close with a sustained run from the back.
scenarios.body: If Ostend goes too steady and sets an insufficient gallop, allowing hold-up horses to close with a sustained run from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Blows Up, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Passengerontheship pushes Ostend into a faster-than-sustainable gallop and both front-runners tie up in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: If Passengerontheship pushes Ostend into a faster-than-sustainable gallop and both front-runners tie up in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Race, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If significant jumping errors or fallers scramble the race order and create an unstructured shape.
scenarios.body: If significant jumping errors or fallers scramble the race order and create an unstructured shape.

watchPoints.text: Passengerontheship arrives with three consecutive wins at this trip on Good ground and is weighted to press Ostend throughout — if he travels better than the leader jumping the final fences, he is the most likely winner.

West Lawn will likely be denied his natural prominent pitch by Ostend and Passengerontheship; watch how Charlie Maggs (3lb claimer) manages the first few fences — if West Lawn is forced to settle too far back, his chance is materially reduced.
Buddah Castle is 94 days off the track and has only three similar-ground runs on record with no win or place in those; Brian Hughes could wake him up first time out but the fitness query is real.

Moodofthemoment has headgear retained and a proven hold-up profile, but David Thompson's stable is 0/3 in the last 14 days — monitor market confidence to gauge whether stable confidence matches the form on paper.

Hexham's undulating circuit and Good ground place a premium on clean jumping and jumping fluency at pace; any error at the ditch or open ditch in the back straight will cost horses in this small field significantly.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, and his Good-ground record (2 wins, 6 places from 15 similar-going runs) is solid, but at OR 100 off a 15-day turnaround, the concern is whether he can sustain his front-running role over 2m7½f in a competitive handicap without being swallowed up; tongue-strap applied.

runners_data.name: Nitty Gritty
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Mark Walford whose form string (5P-2U7) shows inconsistency; best recent effort was a second over 2m1f on Good, and this 2m7½f trip on Good looks a step into new territory for a horse who has only modest sim-going figures of 8/15.

runners_data.name: Miss Kassiopi
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton — always a significant booking — partners this 7-year-old who has placed prominently in four of her last five, with a win over 2m on Good; the drop back in OR to 96 and a 41-day break may leave her needing this if sharpness is required, but her form profile suits a controlled-pace stamina test.

runners_data.name: Stylish Recruit
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap applied, and a winner twice over 2m4f on Good for Sandy Thomson; the 15-day turnaround is fine, and two wins and four places from seven Good-ground starts show consistent form at this level, though a recent string of 652 suggests the handicapper has him pegged.

runners_data.name: Jimli's Cave
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose visor is applied again; Brian Hughes is a strong booking at this track, and his 14/15 sim-going record is the best in the field — the concern is that 2m7½f may stretch him given a career best of 2m4f and a current form run of 55.

runners_data.name: Belladinotte
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on Good 19 days ago for Sara Ender, and Harry Bannister continues the partnership; on a going-day profile and an upward OR trajectory (86 now), she is a lively contender if the race is run at a tempo that rewards a horse who travels prominently and finishes strongly.

runners_data.name: Robert d'Ores
runners_data.note: Consistent underachiever at OR 85 — six, seven, six in three consecutive starts suggests he finds a way to finish mid-pack without troubling the judge; tongue-strap and cheekpieces on, and the Bewley family trainer-jockey combination adds local knowledge, but a win-less profile on similar going (0W1P) tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Lady Phoebe
runners_data.note: Back after a 82-day break (longest in the field) and returning from a chase run, which flags fitness risk; a genuine front-runner by nature who won over 2m2f on Good and placed twice on Soft, she is likely to find herself in midfield through competition for early ground rather than through any tactical choice — that positional compromise is a meaningful disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Star Vantage
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Rebecca Menzies who has placed in all five recent starts without winning; the 58-day break and a going record of 0W2P from 8 similar-going runs paint a picture of a reliable but limited performer at OR 83, and this trip looks fine based on a recent fourth over 2m7f on Good.

runners_data.name: Luminaries
runners_data.note: Three wins and five places from nine similar-going runs is an excellent stat for this 9-year-old, but a current form string of 3P99-0 tells its own story of decline; a natural front-runner who will be pushed into midfield by the congestion ahead of him, which is the worst possible outcome for a horse who clearly prefers to bowl along and find a rhythm.

runners_data.name: Twoplacesatonetime
runners_data.note: Two unseated rider runs in his last three outings are a significant safety concern and make him difficult to trust at any price; Rebecca Menzies has another runner (Star Vantage) in the race, and his hold-up style over this trip on Good has produced one win from limited similar-going starts.

runners_data.name: Myfavouritesister
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural rearward position will be further compressed by redistribution, meaning she races out of her preferred rhythm; the form string (U43P-7) is uninspiring, and while Charlie Maggs claims 3lb, the combination of style compromise and modest recent form suggests this is tough for a 7-year-old at OR 74.

runners_data.name: Dartmhor
runners_data.note: Longest-absent runner in the field at 88 days, and a sim-going record of 0W0P from 3 Good-ground starts makes him a significant unknown; the 6-year-old is lightly raced and has placed on Heavy and Soft ground, and while Danny McMenamin is capable, the combination of absence, trip and going profile makes him hard to assess with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Jeteye is the only confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with a confirmed style fit of 0.92, is likely to stride on and control proceedings at what should be a measured, sustainable gallop over this demanding 2m7½f trip on Good ground. Miss Kassiopi, Stylish Recruit, Belladinotte and Robert d'Ores will push for early prominent positions just behind, meaning the near-side of the field will be reasonably well populated from the off, but the pace itself is unlikely to be frenetic. The field holds more genuinely prominent types than the race shape can accommodate in those front positions — Lady Phoebe and Luminaries are natural prominent racers who will be squeezed into midfield by competition for early ground, while Myfavouritesister and Dartmhor are true hold-up types similarly displaced rearward on the map. With one front-runner setting a controlled, uncontested tempo over a searching trip, this race shape strongly favours patient, prominent-to-midfield horses with proven stamina who can travel smoothly and attack from a position just off the pace into the straight — aggressive closers dependent on a strong gallop are less favoured given the likely moderation in tempo.

watchPoints.text: Jeteye sets the entire pace architecture — if he is slow away or jumped past early by Miss Kassiopi or Stylish Recruit, the expected controlled front-running scenario unravels and the race becomes a scrappy contest with no true leader.

Lady Phoebe and Luminaries, both natural front-runners, will attempt to push forward at the start and could create a brief flurry of early pressure that unsettles Jeteye's rhythm before they are inevitably shuffled back to their mapped positions.

Twoplacesatonetime has unseated in two of his last three runs — watch the early stages for his behaviour at hurdles, particularly given the congestion this large field will create at the first flight.

Jimli's Cave (Brian Hughes, visor, best sim-going record in the field) is the hold-up horse most likely to outperform his mapped position if the pace holds genuinely — he is the one to watch from the rear if Jeteye does set a strong tempo.

Belladinotte won 19 days ago and is on a hat-trick bid — monitor whether Harry Bannister attempts to creep into contention earlier than expected, which would signal confidence and represent a tactical shift that could compress the finish.
